target_customer: Software and remote teams that run async standups and check-ins inside Slack, Teams, Google Chat and Discord
problem: Daily standup meetings waste time for distributed teams; Dailybot runs async check-ins in chat and now also tracks AI agent progress.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per team or user

founders.name: Mauricio Morales
founders.background_notes: YC page: 15 years building internet products, product management at several startups that scaled and were acquired.

founders.name: Sergio Florez
founders.background_notes: YC page. A third-party profile says he started the prototype at a Rocka.co internal hackathon in 2017; that source was not opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: Chat bot integrations with scheduling and summaries; Slack and Teams APIs, standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Many similar standup bots existed and the product category was easy to copy; stickiness came from embedded team workflows.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found on platform owners copying it; the company grew to claim 8,000+ teams and launched Dailybot 3 for AI agents in April 2026.

market_need_then: Remote work growth in 2020 and 2021 drove demand for async standups; product launched on Product Hunt for Slack, Teams and Gmail before YC.

identity.voice_and_tone: Product-led and practical; positioning One place for team updates, AI reports and agent activity

branding.community_and_virality: Listed on Product Hunt with multiple launches and claims 4.8 from 100+ reviews on its site; no merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name that fits the product, with customer logos displayed on the site but no independent brand press found.

outcome_analysis: Dailybot is an active small company that has kept growing a chat based coordination product for several years and recently moved into AI agent reporting with Dailybot 3. Funding is only seen in aggregators, suggesting little outside capital, so it looks capital efficient. There is no sourced acquisition or shutdown, and competition from other standup bots was heavy.
notes: CB Insights lists a 500K convertible note dated September 3, 2021 from Y Combinator, Extruct says pre-seed August 22, 2021, and Startup-seeker says 130K; all aggregators and unverified, so not recorded as a round. Founded year not stated by an opened source (CB Insights says 2020, third-party says 2017 prototype). Competitors list empty because the available Geekbot and Standuply comparison pages are dated 2023 to 2025, not near the 2021 batch; the Dailybot YC launch post was not opened. Completeness pass: the 500K convertible note is recorded from CB Insights alone (single database); Extruct dates a pre-seed 2021-08-22 and Startup-seeker says 130K.
